title: Every infinite law on the tree of names has a solution that repeats nowhere
subject: Boards made of identity distinctions on the words of F2 under Leibniz's rule; shifts of finite type on free groups
conclusion: Every infinite shift of finite type on the free group F2, over any finite alphabet, has a solution with trivial stabilizer, so under Leibniz's rule the tree is a board exactly when a law with finite windows has infinitely many solutions, and no such law forces the plane. A level law on Z/3 with solutions has no finite board exactly when its solutions drift up or down.
